text: After Physarum was trained with cold shocks every 60 minutes and the shocks then stopped, it spontaneously slowed at roughly 60-minute intervals for a few cycles. What mechanism did Saigusa et al. (2008) propose for this apparent anticipation?
choices: Storage of a discrete time-stamp in specialized memory nuclei
Entrainment of the internal cytoplasmic-streaming oscillation to the stimulus period, which persists after the stimulus ceases
A heritable genetic mutation selected for during the training period
Classical conditioning that linked cold to an unrelated chemical cue
explanation: The proposed mechanism is entrainment: the periodic cold shocks phase-locked the intrinsic streaming oscillation to the 60-minute period, and that oscillation kept running (like a pushed pendulum or a struck tuning fork) after the shocks stopped. This is dynamical rather than a discrete stored time-stamp (choice 0), it is not a genetic change (choice 2), and it is not associative conditioning to a separate cue (choice 3).
